### 13.1 Paperclip deep-dive



      <p>
        Paperclip is the closest existing project to Papercusp — but the relationship is more competitive than complementary, despite some surface similarities. Critical context: <strong>they explicitly say they are NOT an agent framework.</strong> From their README: <em>"We don't tell you how to build agents. We tell you how to run a company made of them."</em>
      </p>

      <h4>Paperclip's twelve subsystems</h4>

      <ul>
        <li><strong>Identity & Access</strong> — board users, agent API keys, run JWTs, company memberships</li>
        <li><strong>Org Chart & Agents</strong> — roles, titles, reporting lines; pluggable adapters (claude-local, codex-local, cursor-local, gemini-local, openclaw-gateway, opencode-local, pi-local)</li>
        <li><strong>Work & Tasks</strong> — issues with company/project/<strong>goal/parent</strong> links, atomic checkout, blocker dependencies, comments, attachments, work products</li>
        <li><strong>Heartbeat Execution</strong> — DB-backed wakeup queue, budget checks, workspace resolution, secret injection, skill loading</li>
        <li><strong>Workspaces & Runtime</strong> — git worktrees, operator branches, runtime services (dev servers, preview URLs)</li>
        <li><strong>Governance & Approvals</strong> — board approval workflows, decision tracking, budget hard-stops, agent pause/resume/terminate</li>
        <li><strong>Budget & Cost Control</strong> — token + cost tracking by company/agent/project/<strong>goal</strong>/issue/provider/model</li>
        <li><strong>Routines & Schedules</strong> — cron + webhook + API triggers</li>
        <li><strong>Plugins</strong> — out-of-process workers, capability-gated host services</li>
        <li><strong>Secrets & Storage</strong> — encrypted local + provider object storage; sensitive values stay out of prompts unless scoped</li>
        <li><strong>Activity & Events</strong> — durable activity log</li>
        <li><strong>Company Portability</strong> — export/import with <strong>secret scrubbing</strong> + collision handling</li>
      </ul>

      

### 13.2 How Papercusp positions vs Paperclip



      <p>
        Both projects ship a full vertical stack (substrate + control plane + UI + marketplace). The difference is what gets <em>opinionated</em>:
      </p>

      <ul>
        <li>
          <strong>Paperclip's bet:</strong> there's one right way to model an autonomous organization — companies, employees, org charts, goals, governance, budgets. Build that opinionated model well and become the standard for "how AI companies work."
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Papercusp's bet:</strong> there's no one right way. Build the substrate (drift control, structured handoffs, named decisions) with a <em>plugin architecture for everything above it</em> — including the company model itself. Anyone can publish a "harness config" via the marketplace; the best ones win. Papercup-as-AI-company is just one demo; a marketing-agency or research-lab harness has equal standing.
        </li>
      </ul>

      <p>
        Analogy: <strong>Paperclip is Wordpress</strong> — a complete CMS shipped opinionated; you customize via themes/plugins inside their model. <strong>Papercusp is React</strong> — a runtime + framework on which anyone can build CMSes (or non-CMSes); the model isn't fixed.
      </p>

### 13.4 Ideas explicitly NOT borrowed



      <ul>
        <li>
          <strong>Heartbeats as the wakeup primitive.</strong> Pure heartbeats wake every agent on a schedule even when there's no work. Our orchestrator + `pending_events` + event-triggered ticks (§6) is strictly better for our shape: zero idle wakeups, centralized auditing, sequential drift control. Heartbeats win for multi-tenant scale (many companies in one deployment) — not our concern. They win for stateless decentralized agents — out of scope.
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Their company-as-org-chart abstraction.</strong> CEO → CTO → engineers is opinionated about what an autonomous org looks like. Papercusp leaves that to plugins.
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Their goal hierarchy at the company level (CEO breakdown → CTO breakdown → …).</strong> Adopt parent-link on tasks (yes), but not the org structure.
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Mobile UX as a first-class concern.</strong> Useful for them (operators monitoring 20 companies). Papercusp's reference runtime is ops-shaped, not mobile-shaped. May change.
        </li>
      </ul>

### 13.5 The original Claude-Code framework survey (2026-04, historical)

Before the first harness generation was written, 11+ Claude-Code agent
frameworks were surveyed. This is the survey that shaped the original design;
it's preserved here because the borrowed patterns still run in today's engine
(each mapped below). Star counts, project status, and authorship are as of the
survey date.

| Framework | Core idea | Pattern adopted |
|---|---|---|
| gstack | 23 role-based slash commands, "boil the lake" | "Boil the lake" (do fewer things perfectly) in role prompts |
| Superpowers | 7-phase TDD iron law | TDD iron law in the validator |
| GSD | Per-phase orchestrators, state-to-disk | Fresh contexts + cache-stable prompts |
| Agentwise | 8 specialist agents in parallel + dashboard | Real-time dashboard |
| Hermes | Autonomous orchestration with checkpoints | Named checkpoints *(since deprecated → `needs-human` plan items)* |
| Multi-Agent Ralph Loop | MemPalace 4-layer memory | Layered memory (raw → summary → MEMORY → identity) |
| ComposioHQ Agent Orchestrator | Git worktrees per parallel agent | Worktrees per lane *(now transient scratch worktrees)* |
| OpenSwarm | Linear-driven Worker/Reviewer pair | rejected — no external task source |
| Conductor | Two-mode parallelism | Competition mode *(since removed → work-item redundancy)* |
| claudecode-orchestrator | "Quality through truth" + service smoke-test | Evidence rule + smoke-test gate |
| MOLTRON | Self-evolving Skills.md | `TRICK:` observation-promotion convention |

The ecosystem clustered into **skill packs** (gstack, Superpowers, GSD —
human as orchestrator, one task at a time) and **multi-agent runtimes**
(Agentwise, Hermes, Conductor, ComposioHQ — parallel agents, but each tied to
*their* opinion of how the org should work). The harness took a third
position: a small supervised loop with no opinion about the company, only the
agent runtime — a bet the current blueprint-driven engine still embodies.

Patterns rejected then that stayed rejected: external task sources
(Linear/Notion), vector-DB memory for the inner loop, tmux/Discord/Slack as
control surfaces, agents rewriting their own prompts (audit + determinism
won), and AutoGPT-style infinite loops without decision verbs.

Where the surviving inventions live now:
[decision telemetry + ghost rate](/internal/docs/harness/decisions-timeline),
the [validator's evidence rule](/internal/docs/harness/roles),
[fresh contexts](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/fresh-contexts) +
[prompt-cache discipline](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/prompt-cache),
the [curator](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator), and the
[full decision log](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/log).
